title: Why Humans Overlook Subtraction Even When Less Works Better
alt_title_1: The 2021 Nature Study Showing Why We Add Clutter by Default
alt_title_2: Via Negativa: Gain Focus and Margin by Removing One Piece
description_hook: Across 8 studies published in Nature in 2021, Gabrielle Adams, Leidy Klotz, and colleagues showed that people systematically overlook subtractive solutions even when removing pieces is faster and cheaper. Here is the Minus-One rule for wealth and focus.

scenes.headline: Why Smart Brains Default to Adding More
scenes.stat_label: OUR BLIND SPOT FOR SUBTRACTIVE FIXES
bullets: Wobbly Lego bridge? Most people buy extra bricks
Removing one support brick fixed it for free
scenes.narration: Ask smart people to fix a wobbly Lego bridge, a cluttered schedule, or a bloated budget, and almost everyone adds more.

scenes.headline: Adams & Klotz's 8-Experiment 'Nature' Paper
bullets: Tested across designs, essays, recipes, and schedules
Subtractive fixes rarely came to mind unprompted
scenes.narration: Across eight experiments published in Nature in 2021, Gabrielle Adams, Leidy Klotz, and colleagues found humans systematically overlook subtractive changes, even when removing one piece is faster and cheaper.
scenes.source: Adams et al., 'People systematically overlook subtractive changes', Nature (2021)

scenes.headline: Busy Brains Pile New Apps Onto Broken Systems
scenes.left_body: Stacking new trackers & side hustles onto leaky overhead
scenes.right_body: Cut 1 recurring bill + 1 status meeting -> instant margin
scenes.narration: Under mental overload, that additive bias gets worse: we pile new productivity apps onto broken routines and stack side hustles onto leaky monthly overhead.

scenes.headline: Taleb's Via Negativa: Delete Before You Add
scenes.stat_label: REMOVING FRICTION COMPOUNDS WITH ZERO UPKEEP
scenes.stat_subtext: Every deleted drain permanently raises baseline cashflow & focus
scenes.narration: Adopt Nassim Taleb's Via Negativa rule: before adding any new habit, tool, or expense, delete one recurring obligation or bill that drains your baseline energy.
scenes.source: Nassim Nicholas Taleb, Antifragile (2012), Via Negativa

scenes.headline: Run the Minus-One Prompt Today
bullets: Ask: What can I remove to solve this for $0?
Zero-maintenance deletions beat fragile new routines
scenes.narration: Subtract friction first, and your existing focus and cashflow start compounding without a single extra moving part.
scenes.source: Mind & Margin rule based on Adams et al. (2021) & Taleb (2012)
